icp: self-directed retail swing trader with a full-time job
pain_point: Information asymmetry and time poverty — working professionals trade on fragmented, late, or noisy signals while institutions operate with structured research and defined risk, leaving retail traders stuck in a cycle of FOMO entries, missed exits, and emotional burnout
visual_hook: Split-screen smash cut: LEFT — 6:00 AM, dim home office, alarm screaming, trader (30s, wrinkled shirt) knocks over cold coffee onto a keyboard littered with three monitors showing conflicting indicators (RSI, MACD, volume bars all screaming different directions), phone buzzing with Discord 'pump' alerts, eyes bloodshot, hand trembling on mouse. RIGHT — Same desk, same trader, same 6:00 AM: single clean monitor, printed pre-market plan beside a steaming coffee, calm exhale, finger executes a limit order at a precise level, stop-loss and target pre-set, pushes chair back — done in 15 seconds. Whip pan between the two worlds in 2.5 seconds.

scenes.visual: PRE-DAWN CHAOS. Handheld camera, shallow depth of field. 5:58 AM through window. Trader stumbles in, squints at three monitors. Close-up: monitor 1 shows a red 15-min candle piercing VWAP; monitor 2 shows RSI 72 (overbought); monitor 3 shows a Telegram notification: '🚀 BUY NOW OR STAY POOR.' Trader's thumb hovers, hesitates, chases entry at market. Wide: coffee spills. He wipes it with his sleeve, misses the fill, price reverses instantly. Red P&L flashes -$420.
scenes.voiceover: Five fifty-eight AM. Three monitors. Zero plan. You're not trading — you're gambling with rent money.
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Low, dissonant synth drone. Alarm clock blare. Coffee spill splat. Price tick sounds accelerating.

scenes.visual: LUNCH BREAK BATHROOM STALL. Fluorescent hum. Trader perched on closed toilet lid, phone inches from face, sweating. Screen: red -$1,200 intraday. He's averaging down a moving average crossover that failed. Thumb types 'HODL' in a group chat. Someone replies 'paper hands.' He slams phone against thigh. Muffled coworker laughter outside the door. He flushes without using the toilet — just to mask the sound.
scenes.voiceover: Lunch break. Bathroom stall. Averaging down a loser because a stranger on Discord said 'diamond hands.'
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Bathroom fan drone. Muffled office chatter. Heartbeat thump in sync with red ticks.

scenes.visual: LATE NIGHT RECKONING. 10:43 PM. Dark room lit only by screens. Trader scrolls through the day's trades: 7 entries, 2 winners, 5 losers, max drawdown -3.2%. Journal notebook blank. He rubs face, opens YouTube: 'How to swing trade for beginners 2026.' Autoplay: '90% of traders fail.' He stares at reflection in dark monitor — hollow eyes. Phone lights up: a different notification. Clean. Professional. No emojis.
scenes.voiceover: Ten forty-three PM. Blank journal. Seven trades. Two winners. The algorithm doesn't care about your effort.
scenes.on_screen_text: BEFORE: 10:43 PM • 7 TRADES • 2 WINNERS • EMPTY JOURNAL
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Drone resolves to a single piano note. Keyboard clicks. YouTube audio faint. Then — a clean *ding* notification sound. Sharp. Different.

scenes.visual: THE SHIFT. Extreme close-up: thumb taps notification. Screen expands: CrowdWisdomTrading alert card — 'PRE-MARKET BIAS: LONG XYZ • KEY LEVEL $47.20 • RISK $0.80 • TARGET $49.50 • CATALYST: EARNINGS MOMENTUM + INSTITUTIONAL FLOW.' Trader's pupil dilates. Shoulders drop. Exhale. Camera pulls back: he prints the card. Places it beside monitor. Deletes two of three chart layouts. Keeps only price action + volume.
scenes.voiceover: One alert. Defined risk. Defined target. Institutional flow — not influencer noise. This is what the 4% see.
scenes.on_screen_text: THE SHIFT: DEFINED RISK • INSTITUTIONAL FLOW • NO GUESSWORK
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Piano note blooms into warm, steady ambient pad. Paper print *thwip*. Mouse clicks — deliberate, slow.

scenes.visual: AFTER — MORNING EXECUTION. 6:00 AM. Same desk. Single monitor. Clean chart: XYZ gapping up, pulling back to $47.20 exactly. Limit buy resting. Trader sips coffee, reads Wall Street Journal. 9:31 AM: fill confirmation. Stop-loss $46.40. Target $49.50. He closes laptop. Walks to window. Sunrise. Checks watch: 9:32 AM. Day job starts in 28 minutes. He's already done.
scenes.voiceover: Six AM. One setup. Filled at your price. Stop protecting you. Target rewarding you. Back to your life by 9:32.
scenes.on_screen_text: AFTER: 6:00 AM • 1 SETUP • FILLED • DONE BY 9:32
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Warm pad continues. Birds chirp outside. Coffee sip. Laptop *thunk* close. Calm breath.

scenes.visual: LUNCH BREAK — RECLAIMED. Bright cafeteria. Trader laughs with colleagues, eating actual salad. Phone face-down on table. Buzz. He glances: green +$230. Swipes away. Returns to conversation. Coworker: 'You actually relaxed?' He grins: 'Plan worked. Now I eat.'
scenes.voiceover: Lunch is for eating. Not sweating a screen. The trade manages itself — because you managed the risk before entry.
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Office ambience. Clink of fork. Notification *ping* — pleasant, major key. Laughter.

scenes.visual: EVENING REVIEW. 8:00 PM. Kitchen table. Journal open: four entries this week — three green, one small red (stopped at -0.8% per trade). Equity curve: steady stair-step. Trader high-fives kid running past. Partner pecks his cheek. He closes journal. Laptop stays shut. TV on: movie night. Text on screen fades in: 'Information asymmetry closed. Time reclaimed.'
scenes.voiceover: Three for four. Risk controlled. Journal full. Life lived. This isn't luck — it's access. The same flow the institutions use. Now yours.
scenes.on_screen_text: AFTER: 8:00 PM • 3/4 WINNERS • RISK CONTROLLED • LIFE LIVED
scenes.sfx_or_music_note: Pad swells warm. Movie theme starts. Kid's footsteps. Kiss sound. Perfect resolution chord.
